utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would remind you that the affirmation that you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday we were discussing what had happened to you before the fall of Vukovar, and then you gave evidence as to what happened on the 18th, and then you gave evidence as to what you began to do on the 19th of November, and you said that you went to the Vukovar Hospital. If I can remind you today, if we can just speak at a slow pace so that everything can be recorded on the transcript. And if I can also remind you that if you're going to refer to any of the four people that appear on that sheet in front of you, if you can try and remember to use their letters. But before we talk about the Vukovar Hospital, I would just like to go back a little bit to the 18th of November when you went to Velepromet for the first time when it was full of people, as you explained. And I would ask that Exhibit 262 be placed on the screen, please. And if we can enlarge it one more level, please. Witness, do you see the picture of Velepromet in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that there were military police guarding the entrance of Velepromet. With the pen, can you mark an arrow as to where that entrance was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. If you will just move the picture just a little bit to the left side so that I -- yes. Thank you. That's good. This would be the entrance right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you mark that with an A, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say the military police were guarding the entrance, what do you mean by guarding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were standing at the gate. There was a gate that would be opened and closed as the buses or the trucks would arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how did you know that these were military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would describe as military police as far as I remember during my service in the army. They usually had white belts that would kind of distinguish them from regular soldiers who had brown belts. They could not necessarily have a different uniform but, you know, it would be different belts, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you mentioned that people were being unloaded from buses, and when you arrived there was at least one bus in the Velepromet compound. Could you put a line where you saw that bus, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can mark that with a B.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you also said that there was a large number of people in the courtyard of Velepromet. Can you perhaps with a large circle of sorts, could you put the area where you saw these people, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were women separated right here against this wall. There were men lined up in lines like this, here and here. And then this whole part right here was full of people. I'm sorry, and behind. Behind this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you can mark with a C the -- the rectangle that you drew to depict where the women were lined up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can mark with a D the locations where you placed the lines for where the men were lined up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can mark with an E the two locations where you saw the other people that weren't placed in those groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What letter, sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The letter E.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: E. Okay. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You also mentioned that men were placed in the hangars in Velepromet when you were there on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you said that there were two guards at the entrance to each of the hangars.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you mark with, say, the letter F each of the hangars that you saw men placed in on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And to the right-hand side of that picture do you see another hangar at the end, or is that difficult to --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to say is it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said that you spoke to your grandmother at Velepromet. Do you remember where you spoke to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. She was held in this building here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you mark that build with a G, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: With the letter G.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you speak to your grandmother inside that building or outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were you able to see how many other people were in that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this -- building has two levels. There is a basement level that you can see right in front over there. There was a huge entrance right about here, if I remember correctly. And there's a top level or the first floor where you could see a lot of people in -- well, there's no -- there's no walls or anything so you can see people in there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the basement level, with those two lines does that mark the entrance to the basement or just where the basement --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that would be the approximate location to the entrance of the basement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can mark that with an H, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said -- firstly you testified that men were lined up. Do you know whether men were questioned on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, sir, yes. I heard a lot of people were questioned. Or I think -- my general understanding is that everybody got questioned, not -- nobody was released without questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know who they were questioned by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding was Mr. Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Are you able to say where the men were questioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Can we move the picture a little bit to the side?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps if we not move the picture because we'll lose these markings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see, okay. It's visible a little bit over here, right at this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can mark that with an I, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how do you know men were questioned in that -- in that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will be exhibit number 277.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, you testified yesterday -- yesterday that you went to the Vukovar Hospital on the 19th of November, and you said that you went there to search for person B's parents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What did you do when you first got to the Vukovar Hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were really amazed that -- how many people we had seen on the streets that only by walking towards the hospital. It was all in ruins. It was really hard to recognise the city at all. But when we got in front of the hospital, there were already some people over there. I would say Territorial Defence people. And person B asks, you know, is it possible, did they see any people coming out of the hospital, and -- since he was looking for his parents, and they said well, he wasn't really sure were they dead or alive, so he didn't leave any possibilities. Everything was -- all options were open. So somebody said, "Well, there's some dead bodies across the street if you want to go and take a look at it in those two" -- there were two houses full of dead bodies. So that's what we did first. We went over there will and looked at each one of those dead bodies. But we didn't find anybody that was any resemblance to his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say that there were some dead bodies across the street, was that the street in front of the hospital or behind the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- that's the street right in front of the main entrance of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say two houses were full of dead bodies, where were these dead bodies in relation to the houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first house, which is right across the street from the main entrance to the hospital, there's just a wall and the yard inside, and that yard was full of dead bodies covered with the white sheets. And the second house is right beside, and my understanding was that there was a part of the Croatian police building, and inside the yard or courtyard was all packed with the -- with the dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In relation to the first building where the bodies had white sheets over them, about how many bodies did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say approximately, let's say, 20 to 30 people. Mostly men, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in relation to the second house, about how many bodies were in that yard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even more, but those bodies were not covered by anything. They were just -- I guess they just placed them over there. Nobody was covered. They were just lying down on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were they men or women or mixed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were mixed, I would say, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: After you looked through -- or looked at the dead bodies and realised that person B's parents weren't there, what did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went straight to the hospital. We -- actually, we went to the main entrance of the hospital, to the main gate, which at that point person B was trying to get into the hospital and see, because we knew that there were people inside. So he was wondering if he can get in -- into the hospital at that point. He would --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you say --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you say that he was trying to get inside, how was he doing that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was -- there were military police at the gate or at the main entrance of the hospital. He asked to get in. He was told he has to leave the weapons if he wants to get in, which he did. He left the weapons, but then just a couple of seconds later said -- they changed their mine. They said nobody gets in the hospital. Nobody's getting inside the hospital compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you remember what uniforms these military police were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them had camouflage uniforms and some of them had regular JNA uniforms, but they had white -- white belts on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: About how many military police were at the front of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: At the gate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't -- I can't say exactly the number, but let's say between five to 10 at least at the gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said when you first arrived at the hospital you saw some people you believed were from the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: About how many people from the Territorial Defence did you believe were at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, outside the gate the people were walking all over the streets, but I would say -- let's say at least -- at least about 20 people. At least 20 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you said they were walking all over the streets. Where were they in -- particularly in relation to the main entrance of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them were exactly at the -- at the main entrance of the hospital, and some people were just arriving or somebody was coming from -- there were -- people were coming from all over the sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were the military police letting anyone into the hospital that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that point, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And inside the yard of the hospital, did you see anything or anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen some vehicles inside destroyed. I've seen some stretchers inside, and I've seen some soldiers inside. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what type of soldiers were these people? What group did they appear to belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some of them had camouflage uniforms inside. Some had regular JNA uniforms, but I would say the JNA. I would believe that they were JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And where were they in relation to the yard and the hospital and the hospital building it self?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were right on the main door -- main road as you entered through the main gates of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Was there anyone there that appeared to be in charge inside the yard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have noticed a very distinctive gentleman. He was a real -- to me at that time seemed like a real, real officer, officer in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you say you saw a real officer in charge, what do you mean by that, "real officer"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean that he was distinctively different than any other person that was around him. He was -- he had that kind of real look as -- as a military officer, a JNA military officer, somebody that you would admire as a military. And me having a background of serving the army, I know how the real officers look like.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what did he look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a real, real tough standing. He was a very tall person in camouflage uniform with a Tito hat on his head. He had a military -- well, officer brief -- brief-case or the bag that usually the officers would wear only, not the regular soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say he had a -- a brief-case or bag that usually officers would wear only, where was that on him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing it I guess across his chest, on the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what would that bag be used for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, as far as I can remember from serving the army, I believe that that would be for maps or any other documents that -- that an officer would carry only.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were you able to say what colour his hair was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was dark hair at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what about his height?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a very tall person.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And was there anything distinctive about his face at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed a moustache.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you say that he was a JNA officer. How did you -- how did you determine that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my understanding at that point, because none of the TOs was allowed in the hospital, so I make an assumption and believing that that would be a JNA officer, and from just watching, you know, the way he behaved, you know, and his standing over there as a real gentleman and officer, you know. I would say that would be a JNA officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was he doing when you saw him? You said he was inside the yard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was talking to some -- some soldiers over there. I'm not able to say what they were talking or anything, but I saw him just talking to some soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: How long were you at the front of the hospital by the entrance near the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say maybe the tops about half an hour, maybe -- maybe not longer than that before we went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how long did you see this JNA officer for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that was just kind of brief, maybe a couple of minutes. Just a brief look of a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And why did you leave the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not able to get in to see if his parents were over there, so he decided to go back. We decided, actually, to go back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And why was it that person B didn't want to leave his gun at the entrance to go into the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did in the first place, and then he was not able to get in, so, there was to point of arguing. They wouldn't let anybody go inside the hospital at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If the Exhibit 170, photograph number 3, could be placed on the screen, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the photograph in front of you and do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That's the general Vukovar Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And from that photograph are you able to mark where the entrance to the hospital where you stood at was and where the military police were guarding the entrance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I'm able to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If you can mark that with the letter A, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, it's not working. Sorry. It's not working, the pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If it's got a couple of complications, I can come back to it later. I think I'll do that. Thank you. Witness, after you left the Vukovar Hospital, where did you go from there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We walked back towards the centre of Vukovar. We crossed the bridge, and then we saw the bus, which was empty, and the driver offered us to take us a part of the way back home, which we did. We jumped on the bus and took away -- a part of the way going back. And then we decided to go to Velepromet again to look for his parents, to see what's going on, because people are brought from all over the sites at that point still. So that was the major understanding between us, to go there and see what's going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you got to Velepromet, what was -- what was happening there? And perhaps you can explain it in relation to what had happened the day before, whether there was any different activity and if the scene was any different to the day before when you first went there, when it was full of people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference -- the main difference that I would notice at that point was that the first day when we -- when we were over there people were not allowed to get in, inside, or Territorials were not allowed to get inside with the weapons. They should leave the weapons at the door, at the main door entrance or the gate, and this day was something different. People were getting in and out without some kind of general control. They would just barge in and go out. Still a lot of people coming, coming in and out with the buses and trucks. Some of them were brought by foot. But the situation was not changed very dramatically as far as people coming out and being brought to Velepromet at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you mentioned the day before that the military police were controlling who went in and who left. What were they doing -- well, firstly, were they there --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- the second time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were standing at the main gate as well, but at this time I think there was no more control at that point. People were just coming in and out with weapons or no weapons. There was no more -- there was no more questions, you know, if you want to go in or go out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yesterday -- sorry, on the first day that you went to Velepromet, you said there was a separation of people, separation of men and women. Can you say whether that was happening on the second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the same -- same scenery from the day before. The same -- the same stuff was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you got there, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed at the main entrance. (redacted) got in and went looking for his parents at that point. I stayed over there, and I was approached by one of the soldiers. He left the weapons -- weaponry with me. He told me to go and stand by the -- there was a room just beside the main entrance where some people were held as well. That main entrance was open. I was brought over there, stood in front of the door. There was another guard at that point over there as well. The door was open at all times, and then I looked inside hoping to see maybe my grandparents -- my grandfather maybe was inside. I didn't see anybody that I knew. And then he said to close the door quickly because the press is coming. So -- which I did at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, when you refer to the person that took you out of Velepromet, if we can try and remember to use "person B."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You were approached to stand guard, and you said that you looked inside to see if you could find your grandparents. When you looked inside, what did you see inside that -- that room or building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were about 15 to 20 people, and they were all men, all ages. It wasn't some specific group of -- of elderly people or younger people. They were young or -- and old inside the same room, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how long did you stand guard for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was about, I would say, maybe more -- not more than five to ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was person B doing whilst you were at Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He -- I believe he spoke to his wife or they were looking together because she was working over there as a nurse so she had more access to everybody that were brought to Velepromet. So I guess he just, you know, went to check did they find out anything about his parents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did he find his parents at Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how long did you stay at Velepromet for after you left the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would I say maybe for hour, maybe longer than that. Then we went back. We went back home, all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in terms of military groups that were possibly in Velepromet, can you explain if there was any other military group other than you believe to be the Territorial Defence or members of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in -- inside Velepromet, there were people coming in and out in all -- all kinds of different uniforms. People were wearing even parts of the Croatian military uniforms with no insignia on it, but people were dressed in all kinds of uniforms. I -- I could not say exactly which -- which military they belonged to at that point, but people were just coming and going with all kinds of pieces and parts wearing. I would say mostly TO at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And then when you left, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went back to the house, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the screen is now working and the magic pen, so perhaps if we can look at the screen. This is Exhibit 170, photograph 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you see the picture of the hospital on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The pen now works, so if you could mark the entrance where you saw the military police guarding on the 19th. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Right here. That's the main entrance of the hospital. Main gate. I'm sorry, main gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you mentioned that there was a JNA officer in camouflage uniform that seemed to be in charge. Where was he when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you mark that point with a B, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the area where you saw the military police, can you place an A there, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said inside the yard of the hospital you also saw some soldiers, some JNA soldiers. Approximately where were they inside the hospital yard, and if you could mark that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some people at this point here, and some people right here. Yeah. As far as I could see from where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You also said that the Territorial Defence outside of the hospital. Are you able to mark on that picture the approximate location where some of them were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Some of them were standing at this point. People were looking inside. We were located at this point here. So mostly people were gathered right in front of the main gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you've marked the photograph with -- with dots.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you mark perhaps those two areas with the letter C, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can also mark the areas that you saw the soldiers inside the hospital with the letter D, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And whilst you were there, what were the -- the men that you believed to be from the Territorial Defence, what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some people tried to get in as well as person B. Some of them, they were very rude. They really wanted to barge in -- inside the hospital. They were talking about, you know, they know that Croats were held inside the hospital. They wanted to get in. But, you know, nobody was allowed at that point to go anywhere. So, you know, most of them were mad they can't get in -- inside. But they were standing outside. They were talking about everything, and they were pointing, you know, at the hospital. They wanted to get in and -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say they were very rude, can you be a little bit more perhaps descriptive than that? And the Court is quite used to explicit language. If that in fact occurred.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Pardon my language, but they were saying they want to go in and they want to kill fucking Ustashas, and they know the worst kind are held inside the hospital and they should let them go and get in and do whatever they want to do at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did the military police do anything in relation to these -- this language used by the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they can do much about the language that was used, but they wouldn't let them in. Nobody was allowed to get inside the hospital, no. As far as I've been able to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If we could move to Exhibit 262, please. Oh, sorry, I seek to tender that exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: With the exhibit number -- this will be exhibit number 278, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the photograph on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That's Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You testified that after the hospital you went to Velepromet, and then you were asked to guard a room or a part of the building inside Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you mark -- say, perhaps could you circle the premises that you were actually asked to guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That would be in this proximity here, right close to the exit -- to the entrance of the Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you mark that with an A, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will be Exhibit 279.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, you said that after going to Velepromet on the 19th you went back to the house. And before we start to talk about what happened on the 20th of November, I would like to ask you who was staying at the house on the night of the 19th, before the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'd ask that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Why did person B, why did he go back to Velepromet that night, the night of the 19th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He believed in different things than -- than other people, I think. He was kind of an eccentric as far as some things. He didn't believe in injustice. He -- if he saw some of his friends, he would just -- he would do anything to get them out and save them. I saw him so many times, you know, giving out his cigarettes even to people that he didn't know who they were, or whatever he had in the pockets while we were, let's say, walking to the Velepromet. He just couldn't stand injustice. He couldn't bear that people got beaten or anything like that. He just -- he was just a different person, a person with his own beliefs, and he wanted to do what he believed that was right at that point and that's what he did. He saved me and brought these people as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And person B, he was a Serb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And those five Croat men, they stayed the night at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They stayed two nights with us, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Now, I would like to talk about the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Obviously that night there was quite a number of people staying in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a crowded house, yes, I can tell that. We were sleeping all on the floor with a blanket on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: On the -- on the morning of the 20th, can you tell the Court what you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we usually, during the days that I stayed over there, usual exercise for everyday would be like waking up at around 6.00 in the morning. I would stay in the house and usually we would go about our military duties as well as that day we woke up at 6.00 in the morning. That became some kind of a routine. Person B left. I don't know where or what he was doing at that point, but he came back later on that morning. I would not be able to say exactly the time, but I would say, let's say, around 9.00, 9.30. That's as far as I remember is the beginning of that day. And then he said if I want to go with him to the friend's house so we can have a coffee or something, which we did. At that point, we sat -- we sat in the car. We drove to this -- his friend's house, which is not far from Velepromet at that point, and we sat there for I can't say exactly the time, but we sat over there. We had coffee, and then we heard some woman screaming outside the house. Apparently what I understood from the story that the -- of his friend that we were sitting in his house, she lost her husband during the war. He got killed. So she was screaming like that she heard that Croats are taken out of the Vukovar and they are not going to be prosecuted. They're just going to let them go all, and she was just -- I don't know what she's in -- whether she is in pain or she's really -- I don't know what was going on. She was just out of control.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did she tell you how she knew that Croats were going to be taken out of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. She didn't say anything like -- as far as that goes, but words -- this is a very small town, especially the parts where we were. Like the rest of the town was not inhibited [sic] at all, so, you know, word was spread very fast if anything happens or anything significant is going on. So I guess that's how she found out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I think the transcript is a little bit incorrect. I think you said the rest of the town was not -- was inhibited or inhabited?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were not people living just in this part where we used to -- where we were living. The other part of the town was pretty much empty. There was no people living inside the town because it was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So in the part of the town that you were living in, Petrova Gora --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- were there people living there or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Yes, yeah. But for the rest of the town, I mean towards the centre of Vukovar, that was all empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And is that the part that you're saying was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So once this woman had told you and person B that Croats were to be taken out of the town, what did -- what did you do? What did you and person B do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we -- we got in the car where he said, you know, let's go and see what's going on. We sat in the car. We went -- we drove straight to Velepromet, because there was -- at that -- at this point that was the only point of -- where people were brought, brought in, and so if you want to see somebody or someone, that would be the place to look for them at that point. So as far as we understood, they were bringing more people, and as we knew the hospital wasn't evacuated at that time, so we thought these people were coming from hospital to the Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what were -- what was person B planning to do by going to Velepromet, and what were you planning to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he wanted to see if among those people, because we didn't know who was in the hospital, maybe his parents or somebody that he was looking for. He wanted to see if they're among those people that they're bringing out. So we went to Velepromet to see if there is anybody. But when we got over there, there was nobody. We stayed for maybe short period of time, and in the -- in that time, he heard rumours that people are getting brought to -- to the military barracks, which -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you -- did you go inside the gates of Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that day. Not that -- at that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were you able to see how many people -- I think you said there was nobody in Velepromet. Were you able to see that or were you told that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was nobody brought at that -- at that time, but there were people inside the compound, yes. Because you can see through the gate. The gate is -- it's not kind of closed type of gate. You can see through. So, yeah, there were still people inside. But nobody was brought at that point of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in terms of the large numbers of people that you saw at Velepromet on the day before and the day before that, what was the size -- or what was the size of the people, the group of people that was inside Velepromet at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number decreased. I didn't see that many people inside, but there were people. There were some soldiers. I would believe that would be TOs. And there were people still inside but not as large numbers as the day -- the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what about at the entrance to Velepromet? Was that guarded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was still the same picture with the military police at the gate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And so where did you go from Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He found out that apparently they're being brought to a military barracks. We got in the car again, and we drove to -- to the military barracks. We didn't go in because from the road you could see there was nobody there. Pretty much was abandoned place, as far as we could see from the road, from the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And which military barracks were these, and about how far away from Velepromet were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say if you would walk, they would be about maybe five minutes' walk, not even that. So it took about a couple of minutes to get there with the car. And it's on the main road where -- where the Velepromet is as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And which military barracks were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: JNA military barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you said that when you got there nobody was there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you look inside the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We looked from the road. We didn't see anything. Usually if they were bringing anybody or if anybody was brought usually you would see some kind of trucks or the buses but we didn't see anything at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Had you seen anyone brought to the military barracks before in trucks or buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So how long did you stay at the barracks for, and then what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, we just stopped on the main road. We looked at it and then we went back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at home before you did something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very long. We went back very shortly after that. We returned back to the barracks. We returned back to that main road that leads to Velepromet and then which leads to barracks as well. So we went to the barracks first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And why did you go back to the barracks shortly after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as he understood that they're bringing people to the barracks, so he stopped there first, and then the next -- the second time when we arrived over there we seen totally different scene at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And perhaps if you can tell us what you saw when you went back to the barracks for the second time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point we wanted to get in with the car. There was some kind of a barricade in front of the main entrance or that main road that leads inside. There were people stationed over there. They wouldn't allow us to get in with the car, so they made us to park outside on the main road. We stepped out of the car and we walked inside the barracks, and we were allowed to get in with no problems. When we got into the barracks, we've seen the buses parked in a semicircle inside the barracks. There were a couple of military vehicles, and I noticed one tank and a lot of JNA soldiers. Mostly military police at that point. There were some Territorials as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "mostly military police," what type of uniforms were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them had the camouflage uniforms; some of them had regular JNA or green -- olive-green uniforms but with the white belts on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what were the military police doing when you got there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I -- I remember and looking at the buses, two military police officers -- well, two military police soldiers, pardon me, were inside the bus, and two of them were standing outside the bus at each entrance of the bus, guarding. So for each bus over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how many buses were inside the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, if I can remember correctly, five to six buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you remember where these buses were parked or how they were parked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They formed kind of a semicircle around inside -- inside the compound, one after the other, so kind of -- they formed kind of a semicircle, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You also said that there were two military vehicles there when you got there. What type of military vehicles were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One -- one of them parked was -- was a tank, as far as I can remember, and I think one light armoured vehicle, if I would remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what did you do when you got there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First we -- we didn't know what we were allowed to do, but then we started -- we noticed that a lot of Territorials were just walking around the buses, so we started walking around the buses as well. We were looking if we know anybody. Person B was looking for his parents, thinking that they might be on the bus. We didn't see anybody recognisable, or at least I didn't know anybody, but most of these people were in bandages. Some of them were very badly wounded. It was really very hard to recognise anybody through the window of the bus, plus most of them were holding their heads down like towards the seats. So you couldn't even see anybody's face pretty much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what were you planning on doing by walking around the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We just wanted to see who -- who it was, I guess, or just if we can recognise anybody or -- you know, as I said, you know, he was looking for his parents. He was wondering if he can find them over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said there were Territorial Defence members at the -- at the barracks. You also said that there were military police at the barracks. Did there appear to be anyone in charge of the situation at the barracks or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't really -- I'm not really clear about that, who was -- who was in charge, but I would say military police were definitely in charge of -- of keeping the control of the buses and people that were on the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Earlier you said that you saw some soldiers there. Were any officers in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I noticed at least more than one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you -- can you describe that officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of those -- one of the officers that I specifically recall was the same officer that I noticed at the hospital. The other ones I'm not really sure. I didn't have a very good look.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say the same officer that you saw at the hospital, just so that it's absolutely clear, can you give that brief description again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was very tall, in the camouflage uniform, wearing a Tito hat, camouflage Tito hat, very distinctive person. To me he had a lot of -- a huge impression on me as an officer and a gentleman. He looked a real, real officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Just going back to the hospital for the moment. You mentioned that you saw this officer there at the hospital. Was there any other officer inside the yard of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not -- I would not be able to recall that, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was this officer doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived, they were talking. They were inside the compound. There's kind of a little circle, and as far as I noticed they were just talking among themselves. Not very -- I mean, we didn't really pay attention that much, you know, on what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say there was at least one officer, and you've described the officer, who were the other people that he was talking to or that were talking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they were JNA officers. I believe. The reason I say that, because I noticed -- I noticed they had some kind of ranks, but I'm not really sure what it was or who they were. As I said, I wasn't really paying attention. He was the only one who left a huge impression on me. As I said, I admired that person, the way that he behaved himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you say you admired him for the way he behaved himself, what do you mean by that? How was he behaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, his stand and being -- looking as a real, real officer, like a real, real JNA officer, somebody that you would just -- when you look you would have a respect towards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how many were in that group with this -- with this officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean how many officers were -- were there or --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say, if I can remember correctly, at least three.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how far away from the buses were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that far away. That would be -- buses were parked in a semicircle, and as I said there's kind of a little -- a little kind of a grounding circle inside over there where they were standing. So not far. I would say if you want in metres that would be kind of, I don't know, maybe 15 metres. 15 metres from the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And on that day whilst you were at the barracks, did you notice anyone else of authority come into the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very, very shortly after we arrived I noticed Miroljub Vujanovic arriving in his vehicle together with Stanko. Miroljub Vujovic, sorry, with Stanko Vujanovic. I'm sorry. They jumped out of the car, and they went straight on to these officers. That was really noticeable, because they looked really, really mad for some reason. And what I noticed, some kind of a huge argument started as soon as they arrived. They were going back and forth as far as arguing with the JNA officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And who was Miroljub and who was Stanko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding at that point that Miroljub was in charge of the T -- of the Territorial Defence in Vukovar, and Stanko, that he is the leader of a Chetnik group in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were you able to hear why they were mad or what the argument was about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. But you could see it was really visible that some kind of very huge argument is going on between them. It was back and forth. We were not really paying attention what was going on, but I noticed as far as, you know, that argument going on back and forth. I couldn't hear the words they were saying, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how long did that argument going on for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say for a while, you know. They really seemed upset, I believe both -- both parties. They were waving the -- Miroljub, as far as I remember, he was waving the weapons, and he was in those -- having those, you know, hand gestures and, you know, being really upset talking to these JNA officers. What the argument was all about I'm not really -- I'm not really sure, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. And you said that you were looking at the buses to see if there was anyone that you knew was in them. What about person B? What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was what me. We were going slowly together. We would go from one side of the bus to the other side. So he would kind of -- you know, we had a glance on the both sides of the buses. That's how I noticed the guards on the other side by the -- every entrance of the bus, those military police guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did you -- did you see anyone that you knew on the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was my professor was on the bus, and -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If I can stop you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could go to private session for one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you saw your professor on the bus, without using his name, can you explain what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I tried to speak to him through the window. He seemed very scared to talk to me at all. So I said, "I'll go and talk -- I'll ask one of the officers over there if they'll let me come on the bus to talk to you." And -- which -- which I did. I went to the officers. In this case, I didn't ask any -- Miroljub or Stanko or -- I asked the JNA officers in general over there. So nobody specific. Is it possible for me to get on the bus and talk to my professor. And I guess because of the argument or whatever they just said, you know, we'll see and, you know, just -- they just waved a hand at me and -- so I walked from them. I went straight to the bus. I went to the entrance of the bus. There was a guard at the bus entrance. So I said, "You know, can I get on," and he was -- he said, "No, you can't get in. Nobody gets in on the buses." So I said, "Well, the officers gave me permission to get on." So he said, okay, that's fine. You know, I'll let you on. I had to -- so he opened the door, and there was another one -- I don't know was it a Territorial Defence or some reservists or somebody came on. He said, where -- "Where do you think you're going?" And I said, "Well, I'm going to talk to my professor on the bus." So he said, "Oh, so did he ever give you any bad marks while you were in the school? Because if he did, you know, I'll just slaughter him right in front of you." And I -- at that point, I really got scared because I thought I put him in more danger than he was at that -- at that point, you know, just being on the bus at that time. I managed to -- this guard that was at the door, he managed to chase him away. Or he wouldn't let him get on the bus with me. I managed to get in, and I was talking to him for a while and realised that his wife was with him as well, sitting in the same bus -- well, just beside him. And I said that I'll try to do as much as I can to help him to get off the bus. When we finished the conversation, I got off the bus. I went back to these officers, and I said is it possible for this person to be released from the bus? And they were not really interested in whatever -- whatever I was saying. So I asked the person B if he can talk to some of the Territorial Defence people, if they can help. He did, but there was -- there was to response. Nobody was willing to do anything at that point. Nobody -- as far as I got the reply, it was nobody gets off the buses at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: How many times did you approach the JNA officers to get the professor off the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I approached them twice: Once to ask for permission to get on the bus; and the second time when I asked if it's possible to -- for something to be done to get him released, him and his wife, and get them off the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you described the tall JNA officer that you saw at the Vukovar Hospital and then at the barracks. Where he was in relation to the JNA officers that you approached to get the professor off the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. He was with them as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: How far away were you from this tall JNA officer when you were speaking to him on both of those occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was pretty much face-to-face with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did -- did you see any people at all be taken off the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did. When -- when this argument was finished or at least we thought the argument was finished between the TOs and the officers, they all went inside the barracks or inside the buildings behind -- well, from the buses. So they basically left the scene at that point. Then what I noticed there was a minivan that barged in into the compound with a couple of soldiers. I would not be able to recall how many -- how many soldiers were over there, but they all jumped out of the minivan, and I heard from the TOs that were standing over there that they are looking for the Dosen brothers. And they came from Negoslavci, which is a village just beside -- just close to Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "they came from Negoslavci," are you referring to the soldiers or the Dosen brothers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: People from -- that came in with the minivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: These soldiers, could you describe what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing bits and pieces of all kinds of uniforms. That's as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you know the Dosen brothers before you heard their names mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew one -- one of them, yes. He used to be -- he lived in proximity to where I used to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tadija.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were the Dosen brothers on the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point I didn't know, but, yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When did you discover that they were on the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they started unloading them from the buses, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you explain how that was done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. About five or six soldiers got on the bus. It was the first bus in line. They got through the first entrance door of the bus. It doesn't matter -- well, at that point the military police and guards were on the bus but nobody did anything about it. They were taken off the bus one by one, and as -- they would be thrown from the bus. They were not walking from the bus. They were just thrown through the door. As they would fell on the floor by the front rear right tire, they were beaten to death, I think at that point. It was just horribly -- a horrible scene, how they were beating -- beated at that point. I thought they were dead at that -- when they got out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: How many people -- how many of the Dosen brothers were taken off the first bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say it was a horrible scene, if you can briefly describe how many people were involved in the beating and who they were and how they were doing it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some soldiers, they came in on that -- in that minivan, and as well some Territorials were there, but I would describe about at least 10 to 15 people beating them at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how -- how were they beating those two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With anything they had. With their -- with their guns, with metal pipes, with -- with their feet, with their hands. It -- it was just -- it was just horrible. It was -- the scene was just undescribable as far as horror that I've seen there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how long did this beating of these two go on for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say for several minutes for sure, because when I looked at them I thought that they were dead. I thought they're both dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When -- when these two Dosen brothers were being beaten, where were the JNA officers you referred to and Miroljub and Stanko? You said they left at one point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe they were inside the building. I don't know what they were doing over there, but they were not present at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when these soldiers from the minivan came to look for the Dosen brothers, did they speak to anyone to try and find them, or did they appear to know where to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't speak to anybody as far as I've seen from where I was standing, and that was not very far from that bus. And, no, they just barged into the bus and took them away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said there were three Dosen brothers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The other Dosen brother --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- where was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was -- as far as I could see where they went for him, he was badly wounded on a stretcher inside a military vehicle or truck, I would say, truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And where was that truck parked in relation to that first bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Underneath -- how I would describe that? It's underneath kind of parking garage, kind of open parking garage, but underneath the roof of that parking garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Was there anybody else in that truck apart from this third Dosen brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were more wounded people as far as I could see. They were all wearing bandages, or at least they appeared to be all the wounded people, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you say about how many wounded people were in the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be hard to say. From where I was standing, I could see at least, I didn't know, like maybe six -- six, seven people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And briefly what type of truck was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a military truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did they subsequently take this third Dosen out of the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was thrown off the truck and taken away. He was not beaten at that point. I haven't seen anybody beating him over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were any of the Dosen brothers incapacitated at all or -- I mean, prior to being beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean like having handcuffs or anything or --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Appeared to be sick or wounded.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I can remember on the -- I'm not sure on the buses. I've seen the one that was on the stretcher. He only one appeared to me being wounded, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the one that was on the stretcher, was he on the bus or on the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And where was he taken, the one that was on the stretcher?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All three of them were taken into that minivan and they disappeared from the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what type of minivan was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a civilian minivan. I can't remember the colour, but I know it was civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And were you -- were you able to find out where this minivan went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as we could hear the stories after, they were -- they took them to Negoslavci. Is that true or not, I'm not really sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And these soldiers that came out of the minivan initially, you said that they said they were from Negoslavci. Do you know whether they were regular JNA, Territorial Defence, Chetniks as you referred to, or any other group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know where to place them, but, you know, if they were from Negoslavci, as far as to my understanding usually local people were called the Territorial Defence. So I would -- I would probably say the Territorial Defence, but that's -- I'm not hundred per cent sure on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said that you saw the three Dosens being taken off -- or two off the bus and one off the truck. Did you see anyone else get taken off a bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. There was one more person taken off the bus in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you state who that was and how he was taken off the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name is -- I know his nickname only. He was called Faca, F-a-c-a, and his brother Iko, or I-k-o. He was apparently a part of the -- a Chetnik organisation over there, and he came in and took him -- took him off the bus. And he was not beaten or anything. He was just taken off the bus and left over there in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You mentioned that the JNA officers, including the tall one that was at the Vukovar Hospital, and Stanko and Miroljub, they left and went into some building inside the JNA barracks. Did you see any of those people again before you left JNA barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed -- I noticed Miroljub and Stanko coming out from the building -- or coming towards the buses. That's when the engines started on all the buses. And -- but I haven't seen any JNA officers at that point coming towards the buses, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Where did they go, Miroljub and Stanko, when the buses were being started up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They jumped into their car, the one that they came on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know what type of car they had, whether it was of a civilian or military nature.?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would believe a civilian nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You stayed the buses started up. Did they go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not right away, but the bus -- when the engines started they didn't leave right away. First -- it took a couple minutes, maybe, for two -- two kind of military jeeps to arrive which -- which led the convoy outside -- out of -- from the barracks. So they parked first in front of the convoy, in front of the buses, and then the convoy started leaving the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When go these military jeeps arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shortly after I've seen Miroljub and Stanko coming towards the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you describe with a little more detail what type of military jeeps they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I believe -- if I remember correctly, they would be the ones that are called Campagnola, but we usually call them jeeps. It's just a military vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were they hard tops or soft tops or can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't exactly recall, but some of them -- I mean, there were -- there were couple types that -- some of them had hard tops. Some of them had soft tops. I'm not really sure. I can't exactly ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know who was in these Campagnolas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers, but I'm not really sure who they belonged to at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And then did the buses leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The whole convoy left the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said that the Campagnolas were in the convoy, the buses. Was there any other vehicle in the convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was the truck as well, the truck with the wounded people that I described already. So the whole convoy left and turned left towards the Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The military police that were guarding the buses that you first referred to, what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were still on the buses. There was nobody else on the bus except them. They were guarding the buses at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what about the Territorial Defence people that arrived at JNA barracks, what did they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A lot of people started running to their cars -- cars and going after -- after the convoy or in the direction where the convoy was leading to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And which direction was the convoy going, towards town or away from it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was going away from it, towards the Velepromet, which means leading outside the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this is a good moment to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Because of the redaction, we will need to have a half-hour break and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, I just want to clear up just a little confusion that appears on the transcript and the way that it's been recorded, and I'm referring to page 42, lines 5 to 8. Once -- you said that when the buses started up the military police stayed on the buses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And then you testified earlier that there were also Territorial Defence members at the JNA barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What did they do once the buses had started up and the convoy started to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them -- most of the people that I can -- that I could observe at that point started going into their own cars or whatever transportation they had and started going in the direction where the convoy was leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And the pace that you're going at the moment is a good pace, everything is being recorded, so if we can keep speaking at this speed it would be great.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do my best, sir. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what did you do? What did you and person B do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We waited until the convoy left the compound. Apparently the person B found out where the convoy is going -- is being taken, or where the final destination is going to be. We walked to our car, and we started going towards the Velepromet. We stopped at the Velepromet very briefly and then continued in the direction that we understood that the convoy is going to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And where did you believe the convoy was going?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as we understood, as I understood at that point, it was going to Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when did you find that out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We found that out at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And who did you find that out from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Territorials, what people were saying where the convoy is going.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And why did you and person B go to Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the person that I recognised on the bus was still there, and he recognised a couple of people, he wanted to take them off. As far as we understood, there would be another gathering place for people there because people are still coming out from the basements, and they were being brought. So for us that was just another gathering place like at Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Why did you and person B feel the need to take off people from the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I just -- I guess I felt right at the time to help. I don't know how to say, how to describe that. I just -- I just felt right to do it. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have any concerns about what might happen to these people on the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't know anything at that point what's -- what's going to happen or anything. It just -- to us it was just another convoy of people that came out at this point, like at Velepromet, people who were brought to Velepromet as well. So just another group of people that were brought out from the basements, sir, and being taken out of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
