utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I would ask that Exhibit 256 be placed on the screen, please, and photo 13. Thank you. I don't appear to have it on the screen. I have "Private or closed session" on my screen. I'm not sure what ... Yes. We see it now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the photograph on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Where were the buses parked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a semicircle by those buildings over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Could you mark, using the red pen, the line where the buses were parked, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. There was one bus right here. There was another one right there. Maybe not that big, but like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you mark with an A that general area --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- in those rectangles. You said the Dosens were taken off -- or two of the Dosens were taken off the first bus. Can you place a number 1 to indicate that bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You say that the third Dosen brother was taken off a truck that was parked under some sort of covering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you indicate with a 2 where that truck was parked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You say when you arrived you saw the tall JNA officer that was at the Vukovar Hospital speaking with other officers and then eventually speaking to Miroljub and Stanko. Where was that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you've placed a dot. Can you mark that with a C, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you also referred to the JNA officers and Stanko and Miroljub leaving and going to some other premises within the JNA barracks. Can you show the direction in which they left the area where they were initially arguing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 280.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, you said after leaving the JNA barracks you stopped at Velepromet. What was the reason for that briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Person B, as he said, he just wanted to talk to his wife for -- very briefly or whatever the reason was, but we stopped over there very briefly. That was my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you get out of the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Was the car parked in Velepromet or on the road in front?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, on the road in front.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Had you ever been to Ovcara before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- well, maybe I passed by before but not exactly inside any of the buildings that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you heard that the people on the buses were being taken to Ovcara, what did you believe Ovcara to be, the location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew that there was -- some kind of an economy. As far as I understood, it was an economy. That's all pretty much I knew. I know they raised cattle over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you got to Ovcara, where did you park --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- and what did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We parked on the main road, and we arrived just shortly after, I guess, and we parked on the main road. We got out of the car, and we noticed that people one by one were taken off the bus. I noticed at least two buses that were there at the time. There was kind of a form of -- kind of two lines and these people were walking in between those two lines of soldiers or, well, people that were standing over there. They were taken out one by one slowly with their luggage. As soon as they would step out of the bus, their luggage was thrown away from them, and then beating would start. And they went let them run through the whole thing. They had to walk slowly, and -- as they were beaten. That was my main observation at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And where were the buses parked near, what type of premises?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was some kind of a hangar, like similar to the one that you showed on the picture in the barracks. Like some kind of hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you said that there were two lines formed, those two lines of soldiers. Do you know what type of soldiers they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my observation from where I was standing, I would say that there was a Territorial Defence. That's my observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what types of uniform were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had all kinds of bits and pieces of uniform, some JNA, some overcoats. All kinds of -- all kinds of uniforms you could see there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in relation to the hangar, where were -- where were the two lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the two lines were between the bus. So exit of the bus and the entrance of that hangar. So basically this whole kind of short distance between the bus and hangar, that was all blocked from both sides with the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how many soldiers were in these two lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be just a guesstimate. I would say 20, 15, 20 people, maybe more. I'm not sure. There were people standing on the side as well, so I'm not -- I can't say exactly the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said that there were at least two buses there. Were the buses being unloaded at the same time or separately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were unloaded separately and, as I said, people were taken off one by one. So there was not a -- I didn't observe being a group of people taken out at same time, just one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how many people were in these two buses, say in each of the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, each bus was pretty full, as far as I could see from the outside, and the one that I entered in barracks, when I spoke to the person that I'd recognised, as far as I could see all the seats were taken, so I can't exactly saw how many seats was inside, but approximately 40 to 50 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said as these people were taken off the buses they were beaten slowly. Was everyone beaten? Was a few beaten? Can you give us an idea of how many people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every one of them. Everyone that I observed that came out of the bus was beaten. And as I said, they were not beaten slowly. They were -- they were told -- I could hear that they said they can't run. They have to walk slowly as they beat them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what type of beatings were there? Were they using any implements or were they beating with their -- their arms and legs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything. Everything that I could remember. Some -- some people used guns, some people used I guess some kind of pipes or some kind of sticks. Some people that came -- emerged from the bus with their crutches that were taken from them and they beat them with the same ones. Some people would just fall -- just fell on the floor, well, right on the ground, and they would try to crawl inside and they were beaten on -- from all sides with the feet, with the boots, with anything that can hit them on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how long was each person beaten for? Just an average, if you can say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a big distance from the bus to the entrance, so I would not -- I don't know. I can't -- I can't say that. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said when the buses left the JNA barracks the military police were still on each bus.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you see them at Ovcara or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were still on the buses. They were still guarding inside the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What were they doing whilst each of these people were being beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were just inside the bus. I'm not sure what -- whether they were hitting the people or not, but I could see only the bus -- the one closer to me that the person was still standing by the -- by the entrance -- or exit. So I don't know. I can't say for sure what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you say about how long it took for the men on the buses to be placed in the hangars -- placed in the hangar, sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say maybe, I don't know, 15, 20 minutes. Something like that, yeah. Maybe more. I'm not sure exactly about the time-frames, but it took a time for -- for all of them to get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And where was your car parked in relation to the hangar? About how far away from the hangar was it parked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not far. About -- let's say approximately about 20, 25 metres from the -- from the entrance, on the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And where were you and person B doing whilst these beatings were being carried out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Person B was with me by the car for -- for a while, and then he went -- went towards -- towards the entrance of the -- of the -- of that hangar. I stayed by the car, and I was approached by a military police soldier after, I would say, I don't know, 10, 15 minutes, and was told to come with him because they need one more person to stand behind -- behind the hangar so nobody gets out or run away through the windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you remember if person B had gone towards the hangar, gone towards the entrance whilst the beatings was being carried out or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say he entered once during that, but I -- I can't exactly recall. I think he entered inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was the purpose, do you know, of him going inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. At that point I'm not really sure, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you said you were approached by a military police soldier to help stand behind the hangar so nobody got out or ran away; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: This military police soldier, do you remember what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in a JNA -- in a JNA uniform, olive type of uniform, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did you go with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He took me to the back. There were other three people standing over there already.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at the back of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very long. I got -- I got replaced by somebody very, very shortly, so I would say maybe 15 minutes. 15, 20 minutes, tops.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did anyone try and escape --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- from the back of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I haven't see anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And after the 15 minutes, 15 to 20 minutes, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we just -- well, we were just standing over there and when this person showed up, you know, that told me I can go back wherever I came from, wherever it is. So I started slowly walking back around the hangar and going back -- going towards the entrance of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And why did you say yes to going to the back of the hangar and guarding it at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was -- I was just told to go there. I don't know. I didn't -- I didn't object. I'm sorry. I -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you feel you had any choice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you had much of a choice for anything. Like, I mean, you didn't know who -- who was who at that point. It was a chaotic situation, you know. There were just -- some people would just tell you do this, and, you know, I don't know if I have to do it or not. You know, you kind of feel pressure to do it, so, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you said you started walking slowly back around the hangar towards the entrance. On your way back, did you see anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I seen the same JNA officer that I've seen at the -- at the hospital and at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What was he doing when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was -- he looked very angry, and he seemed standing -- he was standing alone. There was nobody with him, just alone on the road towards -- towards the entrance of -- of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you say anything to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I -- I -- as I said, I had a full respect for that person. I said hi to him, which he didn't reply at all. He didn't even look at me. He was just standing there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you got to the front of the hangar, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I entered inside, inside the hangar. Actually, before that I noticed a lot of bags of people thrown on the floor. I noticed some names on the bags. So I looked at the bags first, and then I entered -- entered the -- entered the hangar inside to the main entrance. Actually that was the own entrance to get in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Just before we go -- we talk about what you saw inside, why did this JNA officer appear to be angry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir. He was alone over there. He was standing alone. Why he was angry, that's the impression that I've got, just to -- you know, just looking at him. I don't know. I can't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was the closest distance you got to him when you walked past?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was very close, sir. I came very close and said hi, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you got inside the hangar, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen a lot of people. I've seen a lot of people all over the place. On my left side, on the floor, I've seen people, those kind of badly wounded that I've described, that I've seen, pretty similar to ones that I've seen at the barracks in the truck. They were all lined up and sitting on the floor on the left side right at the entrance. On the right side I've seen the rope placed from one side to the other side of the hangar where I've seen approximately 20 to 30 people behind the rope. As I heard later from people, they said that those are specially trained criminals. Right in front of me there was -- there was kind of a back -- back exit door, and beside that door I've seen about seven -- seven or eight people standing. Those were -- I don't know why, but those were placed separately from everybody else. And then on the left side I noticed people sitting kind of in a ways -- like, in lines but they were all sitting on the floor. That's the first -- that's the first picture that I've got from the inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Apart from people in the hangar, was there anything else in the hangar in terms of equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't noticed any equipment at all. There was hay on the floor, but that's all I pretty much remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And as far as soldiers are concerned of any sort, did you see any in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. There were a lot of -- there were a lot of people inside the hangar, yes. People in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And are you able to say what you thought these people in -- who you thought these people belonged to in terms of a general military grouping like we've discussed earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe that majority of them were Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say the majority, do you have any conclusion about who the minority would be, the remainder?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've seen some people that were dressed up in the black -- with the black overcoats, giving me the impression that they belonged to the Chetnik group, but I'm -- I'm not really sure whether they were just wearing -- because at that point there were a lot of people that were just putting all kinds of symbols on themselves. So I can't say exactly they were Chetniks or not, but they were dressed -- some of them were dressed like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to the military police that were on the buses --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I don't know what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you came back from behind the hangar to go into it, were the buses still there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: How long after the buses were emptied did they leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not really sure. I haven't seen them from before -- from behind, no. I don't know. I guess right away. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And whilst -- whilst you were in the hangar, what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just walking over there or talking to the person B.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know what person B was doing in the hangar, what he was attempting to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He picked about 15 people to take them out. He was already -- he already spoke to them, I guess, before -- before I came in, and he had them -- he wanted to take them out, all of them, like all of 15. I believe about 15 people. He had them lined up very close to the left side of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And those 15 people, do you know whether he knew them and why he selected those particular ones?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparent -- as far as I understood, he knew them very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And are you able to say what their ethnicity was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know some of them were Croats, that's for sure, but I can't say for all of them. I can't exactly pinpoint everybody, no. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said that he picked 15 people to take them out. Was he able to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. He was approached by one or two soldiers who started arguing with him, and they wouldn't let him take anybody outside. That's where the argument started and, you know, it was swearing and, you know, this and that, and they were just, you know, going on and on in this argument. And then one of them took the gun out and he said, "I'm going to shoot you, and you're not going" -- you know, "you're not going to do this kind of stuff. This is not a Velepromet," in that kind of sense. And this argument was going on, and then Vujovic got -- Miroljub Vujovic got involved in this whole thing, and when this person took the gun out and wanted to shoot this person B, he said, "No, no." I mean, he kind of interrupted the whole argument and then -- that's when it stopped. That was what was happening at that point that I could -- that I could observe. I was very -- pretty close to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know why the one or two soldiers were objecting to these 15 being taken out by person B? Did they state the reason why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't say the reason why, but they just wouldn't let anybody go outside. They wouldn't let go anybody. What -- what the reason was at that point, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Was person B able to take out any of those 15 people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on he tried to go one by one with them, and, yes, he managed to take three of them outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you were in the hangar --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- did you see anyone that you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I recognised at that person D.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: It's not so clear on the transcript. The person that you recognised - oh, it's now clear - was person D; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how did you know him, just briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know each other from school, from before the war. We hang around together for a while, but we go -- as kids we would go outside and have fun.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you recognised him, did you go and speak to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, sir. I managed to speak to him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was he doing, and what were you saying? Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was sitting on the floor. I hardly recognised him because he used to wear glasses, and at that point he didn't have any glasses on. I asked him what happened to him and what is he doing over there. And he said, "I don't know. I got separated from my mom." So at that point I said, "Well, you know, if I can help, I'll -- I'll try to do that." And so I did. I went to -- I went to person B. I asked him if it's possible to help this person and get him out of the hangar, and -- which we were able to do it. And he was placed outside the hangar on the left side of the entrance. And then there was another person sitting beside him. He said -- it was very -- he was kind of very young person. He said he's from Zagreb, and he -- that he was forcefully brought to the Croatian forces just a couple of days before fall of Vukovar, and he said he just got a first kid. He recently got married. He started crying, talking to me while I was talking to the person D. He asked me if I can help, and -- which I said, "I don't know if I can, you know. I don't know if I can do anything at all." And in the meantime, a couple soldiers noticed that what we are trying to do, that we are trying to get out these people, so they spoke to the person B, and they said that nobody gets out from there. And then they made some kind of a paper making us sign for each person that we take out from the hangar with our own lives, so that we are going to guarantee for these people that they were not involved in any atrocities or anything during the war. And if -- if that's getting -- if they find out that something -- they did something during the war, that we're going to pay by our lives for that. And we did sign for -- we did sign for all five of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Now, this person D and this other person from Zagreb, do you know what ethnicity they are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that point. I don't think I -- I knew exactly at that point, but he was my friend. But what I said, you know, I just -- I wasn't really sure at that point. I'm not ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the two soldiers that noticed that you were trying to take these two out and asked you to sign for them, do you remember what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By my general understanding from them, they were reservists. They were wearing JNA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how did you get that understanding from them, that they were reservists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said that they were reservists. They came here to fight for Serbia, and, you know, we're not going to take anybody out just like that from the hangar. So that was my understanding. They said it, that they were reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did they say where they were based?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not those people, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were you able to take those two people that you signed for and the other two or three that person B took out of the hangar, were you able to take them with you when you left Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. They were not allowed to leave Ovcara at that point. No. What the reason was for that I don't know, but they wouldn't let us take them -- take them out with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So when you left Ovcara, where were they left --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were left --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- in relation to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were left standing beside the hangar on the left side -- on the left side of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And where did you go when you left Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went straight home. Person B went -- went to talk to his wife about whatever there was, and he said that he's going to bring some people, some more people to the house that night. So, you know, we should prepare more space for them to sleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And I assume back then there was no access to telephones and that type of thing; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you go back to Ovcara after you went to person B's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, we came back. We returned right away. So it was just a brief -- brief stop at the house and we went back to make sure that these people get back. They were -- they're not -- they could come back with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And why did you think that you'd be more successful on this occasion than you were when you first left, when they weren't allowed to go with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but he wanted to go back and make sure that they'd come back with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you got back to Ovcara, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw them standing outside, and very shortly after that, I would say a couple of minutes later, there was a minivan that came in and took them all. My understanding was that they were taken to Velepromet for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Was there any discussion as to whether yourself and person B should take them or whether or not the people that were driving the minivan should take them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no discussion about that. They were just taken to this minivan, and my understanding was that they were taken to Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: At that stage, when you were at Ovcara, were you aware of what was going to happen to the people inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I don't think any of us were aware of what was going on. At least for two of us. I'm not sure for people inside. We glanced one more time -- maybe once inside, but the picture didn't change much. They were pretty much all TOs inside. But, no, I wasn't aware what's going to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the minivan, can you describe that, whether it was more of a military nature or civilian nature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a civilian, civilian minivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the people that took the five men, were they civilians or more military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was more TOs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Once the minivan had left, did you see anything else occurring at the hangar, either inside or out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed there for maybe a very -- very brief short period of time. I noticed a tractor was brought with a trailer and parked in front of the main -- main entrance to the -- to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can just describe the trailer briefly, what it looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a tall trailer with some kind of ladder, I guess, to climb on. I can't remember the colour, but I remember that it was a tall one, covered with some kind of plastic cover on top.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you go inside the hangar when you went back to Ovcara the second time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just once, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And -- and what did you see inside in terms of -- compared to what you saw when you were there sometime earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was pretty much the same picture. I haven't seen anything changed at that point. There were a lot of TOs over there at that point, but I haven't seen anything that's been changed as far as the picture inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: How long did you stay at the hangar on the second occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very briefly. After this tractor was brought over there, we left pretty much couple minutes later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the tractor and trailer that was brought in front of the hangar, do you know who was driving it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I can't recall that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you see anything happen to the tractor and trailer whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you left Ovcara, can you tell the Court whether it was light or dark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was getting dark already. I think it was -- it was getting dark or darker. I'm not -- I'm not really clear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that Exhibit 256, photograph 20, be placed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, just to clear the transcript a little, when you left Ovcara, can you explain what the light was like at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No. On the second occasion. You talked about it getting dark. Can you describe it a little bit more?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was kind of -- well, it was getting dark, yes, or it was already dark. I can't really exactly remember. I think it was dark. I think it was getting dark or dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. If we -- if we could enlarge the left-hand corner of the photograph with all of the premises showing -- if we can continue across. Sorry. That was my mistake. Go back. And just have the hangar and all of the building premises highlighted. Sorry. If we can have the hangar and the premises on the left, if all of that can be enlarged, please. So all the buildings on the photo are enlarged. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, looking at this photograph, do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What do you recognise it as?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's the Ovcara economy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you remember the road that you took to get to Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's the main road that leads from -- how do I -- I think I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you -- with the pen, can you place a red line as to the direction that you took to get to the Ovcara hangar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 281.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if I can ask for the same exhibit, 256, but photograph 22, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, looking at this photograph, could you with the red pen draw the locations of the two buses, at least two buses that you saw there when you first arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One was right there, located, and the other one right behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that's represented by those two rectangles; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Could you draw, say, two double lines showing where the people were beaten as they went into the hangar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can mark that with a B, please. With a C, can you mark the place where you were asked to guard the back of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Right behind here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And with an arrow, can you show the direction that you walked when you went from the back of the hangar to the front?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And with a D, can you show the location where you said hi, or you said hello to the JNA officer that you saw at the Vukovar Hospital and then the JNA barracks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It's right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you mark that with a D, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And with an E, can you mark the place where you first parked your car when you arrived at Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was somewhere here, very close. Almost right behind the buses, like couple feet behind the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if you can could just place the figure -- the letter E, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 282.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, when you left Ovcara for the second time, did you go back to person B's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did, sir. We didn't stop anywhere on the way. We went straight back to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the five Croat men that person B took from Velepromet, were they still staying at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were still with us in the house, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: How long did you stay at person B's house from the 20th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just maybe two or three days, not longer than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And during that two or three days before you left, what were you doing generally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pretty much nothing. We were just in the house or walking around. I tried to salvage some pictures from a house where I used to live, if I could find anything that was available to find and save some stuff that was left over, because everything was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what was your intention at that stage? Where were you going to live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no idea where to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When you were there for that two or three days, was there any -- any conversations about what had happened at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Not -- not exactly in our house, but there was a lot of rumours going on on what had happened to the people that were at Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what were the rumours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding was that everybody got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And who was -- who was spreading this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say Territorial Defence, or people just spread the rumour all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about -- in that time that you were there, about that two or three days, about how many people did you hear that from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I would say a lot. It was kind of the main thing that was happening over there. A lot of people knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And after that two or three days, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I applied for a pass and went back to visit my parents, to go. I got scared of what happened in relation -- what happened at Ovcara. I went -- I went back to see my parents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And why were you scared?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess because I was there. I guess because I was a different nationality, and I guess because I managed -- well, I -- I tried to help some people to -- well, I helped some people get taken from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And why -- why was the fact that you were different nationality, why was that making you scared?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time it was enough for somebody just to point the finger at you and you would just disappear. I don't know. I guess because I was somewhere that I was not supposed to be. That's just my -- that's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you said that you were scared as well because you helped take some people out from there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Why do you think that would have placed you in danger?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because people that were over there, they saw us taking these people outside, and they knew who I was, and -- in relation to my ethnicity. So I was really scared for my life at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you got a pass to leave Vukovar. Who did you apply to that pass -- for that pass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I applied at command in Velepromet to go. You had to -- if you wanted to leave the region, you had to apply for the pass. You cannot leave the region just like that. They always had a control who is coming in and who is leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you left. And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Bijeljina, to my parents, where they were staying as refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Whilst -- before you left, after Ovcara had occurred, were televisions working in the town of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Vukovar, no. We didn't have any electricity. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you arrived in Bijeljina, how long did you stay there for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed maybe for three or four days, no longer than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And were televisions working in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was no war there. That was a normal situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And were you watching the television when you were in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: On the TV were you watching any footage in relation to events that occurred in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. There was a lot of footage all over the place, especially in the news. And the news was, I best, the main -- main -- main thing that was happening on TV at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you explain what type of footage you saw on the TV?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was mostly war pictures from people taken out of the basements, people walking through the streets, people that were coming out of the basements. A lot of war pictures and clips.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier that you saw this tall JNA officer at the Vukovar Hospital, then the JNA barracks, then at Ovcara. Did you ever see him again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not after that, sir. Not in person, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you see him in any other way other than in person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did see him on TV, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when was the first time that you saw him on TV?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got to Bijeljina, first TV news that was shown over there he was -- he was on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in what context was he on TV? What was the footage about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was some kind of footage on -- I mean, I know locations in Vukovar, so one footage that I've seen specifically was with international organisation on the bridge when he was talking to somebody. And the second one inside the hospital, I think talking to reporters or something, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say you saw him inside the hospital, are you referring to the compound or the building itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And can you explain a little bit more in detail the nature of the footage that you saw when he was speaking -- when this officer was speaking to someone on the bridge from an international organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was something about getting the clearance to go to the hospital. If I recall correctly, it was about going through the town to the hospital, about the clearance or getting the clearance to get to the hospital grounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what about the footage where you saw this same person in the compound area of the hospital? Can you give a bit more detail about the nature of that footage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was just kind of -- some kind of interview with the reporters about the conditions in the hospital, I guess, or what's happening in and around the hospital at that -- at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when you came to The Hague just recently and you were being prepared for court, were you shown a series of clips in relation to Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And from those clips did you see any of the clips that you saw when you were in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I've -- I saw two clips that I could recognise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask that if the video clip from 65 ter number 314, if that could be shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: It's in Sanction, Your Honour. And if we can show clip 1, which would be from 17 minutes and 29 seconds to 19 minutes and 40 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: "I was -- I got used to better collaborations [indiscernible]. [No translation]. The problem -- that is the problem. "That is the problem, okay. "The problem is I see soldiers walking on the street. [Indiscernible]. My colleagues were there. [No translation]. [Inaudible]. And his soldiers were killed this night also. We are trying to ensure you security. If you don't like it, you can go back. And [indiscernible] -- because we gave you everything that you asked."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise that clip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that clip, when did you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it on television when I was over there, when I was in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if I can ask that we go back to that clip and just take one still from it of the two men speaking. If we can stop there. Witness, looking at this still from the clip, the person on the left-hand side, do you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how do you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the same person that I've seen in the hospital, at the barracks, and at Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And with the red marking pen, can you place a ring around that person? Oh, it doesn't work. Yes. I don't think it works on the video. And the person you recognised, is he on the left or the right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Wearing the hat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that clip and that still as two separate exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are we able to identify the point on the time recording of the clip?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's 5 minutes and 9 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I thought this was between 17 minutes and 29 seconds and 19 minutes and 40 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct. And -- sorry, it's 5.9 seconds after --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The commencement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The commencement, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the video clip will be exhibit number 283, while the still will be exhibit number 284.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if I can ask that we show part of the same 65 ter number 314 and the clip from 21 minutes and 9 seconds to 22 minutes and 34 seconds. Witness, we'll play this clip and I'll ask you a couple of questions about it in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: "And there was their duty and they should have done this job properly. No one [indiscernible]. [No translation]. There was no -- there was -- there was no -- there was no misunderstanding. [No translation]."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise that film clip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And where do you recognise that from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the compound at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And have you ever seen that clip before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen it in Bijeljina, yes. I've seen it on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the JNA officer that was in that clip talking --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- did you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And who did you recognise him as being?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His full name or --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I found out. Yes, it's Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you know his full name before you got to the Vukovar Hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: On the 19th of November?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that film clip, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: It is from 21.05 to 22.34.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number 285.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, between 1991 and 1992, from the time that you left Vukovar and went to Bijeljina, for, say, that nine months, what were you doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was trying to say away as much as I can from Vukovar. I would come in maybe two, three days and then I would leave for a month or two and then come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And why did you try to stay away as much as you could?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was scared for my life. I was scared because of the things that I heard that happened at the Ovcara. I was scared for myself as far as being a different ethnicity and being -- witnessing something that -- that I was there and that I could confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And during that time that you visited Vukovar in that -- in that period, the 1991, 1992 period, were you ever directly threatened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Couple of times by some people that they were present at Ovcara, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, if we could go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Given the time, this would seem an ideal moment for the break, and we will resume at a quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. My name is Vladimir Domazet, on behalf of Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I not get the English translation? I understand everything the gentleman is saying, so if you can leave the Serbo-Croatian there, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you want to hear in Serbo-Croatian or in English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Croatian-Serbian, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you hear me now? At the outset, I have several questions about your personal details, and in order to comply with your protective measures, I seek that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I will now ask you a couple of questions about your regular military service with the JNA. You say that you joined the JNA sometime in September 1990. The first place you went was Slavonska Pozega where you spent about three months; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: That means that it was towards the ends of that year or the beginning of the following year that you got a transfer to Kranj, Slovenia; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: As you said, as early as in January 1991, that you went on furlough; you went on a leave and went home. This seems to be exactly the same time you arrived to Kranj. Was this a regular leave of absence or something exceptional?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was -- it was just a regular leave or something. I'm -- I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You travelled with some other soldiers, specifically you probably had to change trains in Vinkovci, and there were three of you. You were with two other soldiers; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. It was me and -- yep, it was. That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were you all wearing your JNA uniforms as you were travelling, or were you travelling in civilian clothes, which would also have been possible according to the regulations that applied.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, in -- in the barracks where I served the army, at that time it was not allowed to travel in civilian clothes, but I was -- I was in uniform at the time for what you're asking for, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know the ethnic background of the other two soldiers travelling with you, the soldiers who were with you in Vinkovci when you had that incident with the police there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, they were Serbian nationality, and they were -- one from them -- one of them, if I can remember correctly, was from Subotica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: While testifying in chief, you said that those Croatian police officers ID'd you and subsequently verbally abused you and threatened you. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did they ask you to show any personal documents? If so, which ones did you show, your military booklet or your regular ID?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked for ID first, yeah, and then we -- we showed them -- I had a military book with me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: It was probably based on that information that they drew conclusions about your ethnicity, and that was when the abuse started, I assume. That's what gave rise to the abuse. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. Can we please briefly go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would just add that you will realise that name will not go outside this room. It will be removed from the transcript and from the tape.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: My understanding is these police officers mistreated you because you were JNA soldiers. That was the chief reason, or at least that's what you believe to have been the case, not because you were an ethnic Serb; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that ethnicity had anything to do with that at that point. It was -- I think that because we were just in uniforms and, yeah, we were JNA soldiers at that time. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you please tell us in the briefest possible terms what the abuse and the threats comprised? What did they tell you as soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what they said first -- first they asked for our IDs, and they wrote -- they wrote down all the details about all of us. And then what happened after that, that -- while they were taking the details about us, they would say all those bad words to us like, you assholes, you should take your uniforms off. You know, you should run away from the army. You know, you won't exist any -- any longer. What are you doing here anyways? And that kind of verbally assaulting you. Nobody was pushed or anything, but -- but it was -- it was really bad words that they used at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: But they still took your personal information for no special reason. I don't think you provoked that measure in any way, and you did not reply to their taunts, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't provoke them in any way. Yes, they did take all the details. They took all the details from us, and they wrote down in their books, and they -- they stopped us right away as soon as we stepped off the train, which was very -- really strange to me at that point that civilian police can even ask anything from -- from -- from the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were these regular Croatian police officers or paramilitaries, perhaps, since this is something that was known to happen at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It was a different -- different police. It wasn't a regular police in the blue uniforms. These ones had -- had a grey -- grey uniforms with the Croatian symbols on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So when you say with Croatian symbols on them, which symbols do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Inaudible].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: As you already explained, that same night there was another incident. Before we go ahead with this question, your previous answer was not recorded, when I asked you about the symbols or insignia that those people were sporting. Can you please repeat what the insignia were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had the grey uniforms with the Croatian symbols, and that symbol was a chess field, or "sahovnica" as it was called at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now move on to the next incident which was more important than the previous one. Four persons wearing masks broke into your house that night and kidnapped you. My first question is: Did you notice anyone following you when you were in Vukovar. Did you anyone know you actually reached your house in Vukovar that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I didn't notice anyone following me. But all I know that night is they took all the details where I lived, my address and everything, but that's -- did I notice anybody following me, no, I did not. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: That's precisely why I'm asking. Is it possible that this was a result of the information obtained by those police officers? Is it possible that that was the reason you were kidnapped that same night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a big possibility for me to answer yes, because I didn't have any contact with anybody else that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Although these persons were wearing masks, was there any way for you to tell based on their speech or on their accent who they could have been, your kidnappers other attackers if you like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to tell at that point because I was really scared, plus I was beaten all the way in the car. They were screaming at me that I'm Chetnik, and for whatever reason they would hit me all over the place, wherever they can. If I -- I don't think I can recognise the voice or anything that I would say that was that person or that person. I can't. It's hard to say because I was so scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You answered some questions about this, and you said that both the police and the military police were informed about this. Do you know if any steps were taken against these unarmed perpetrators as a result of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understood from my mother, I don't -- I don't think anything was taken. I don't think anything was done after that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What is the distance between the place you were kidnapped and the forest that you were eventually taken to and abandoned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say about maybe five kilometres outside -- outside Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How did they leave you there? Did they run away for some reason or did they just leave you there? Did they tie your hands so you couldn't move?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. No, sir. I was -- I was unconscious. I'm not sure why did they leave or what the reason was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You spoke about this, but specifically how were you found? Who found you and how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I believe it was civilian police or military police, I'm not sure, but one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was it morning already by the time this happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I really can't remember anymore. I -- it was such a -- traumatic for me that I don't remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. You do remember that you received hospital treatment subsequently. My question is: At which hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Vukovar Hospital, and then after that I was released and went to Ljubljana.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember in which ward and who was your treating physician?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I don't remember, sir. I was -- I don't know. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yesterday, answering to the questions of my learned friend about the length of your hospital treatment, I think you mentioned it was about a week or two. However, in your statement it says a month. It's not really very important, but I would like to know whether you can remember what length of time you spent in Vukovar Hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Vukovar. I'm not really sure. It could be couple days, but altogether, I think in a -- week and a half or two weeks altogether with everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say "altogether," you're referring to the other treatment that you received in Ljubljana; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, altogether. I would say -- yes, I would say altogether, while I was going through check-ups and -- I've been in couple of -- couple of medical centres in Ljubljana, not only because of the injuries -- well, injuries that I incurred in that -- in that incident, but I went through psychological evaluations as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Whereas this in a military hospital in Ljubljana? Were you seen by military doctors when you speak of these tests and examinations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For psychological, some of them were -- some of them were military, some of them were civilian ones, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And what was the final outcome of your medical treatment? What was the conclusion of the medical commission or the doctor about your fitness for further military service in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked after psychological evaluation what would I like to do. It wasn't -- they had an opinion that I should -- I should leave, and I had an opinion that I wanted to leave. Psychologically, I wasn't -- I wasn't really able anymore to serve the army. Physically, yes, but not psychologically. It was a huge trauma on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When being interviewed by the psychologist, did you mention the first incident where you were threatened by policemen as well as the second incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the psychological evaluations and all that stuff, I don't know. They didn't ask me then that kind of questions. They would put all this stuff on my head, whatever. I don't know. I can't remember. But I don't think there were any questions regarding that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. I thought that maybe you had recounted all your experiences before taking these tests. However, if you don't recall the details, I won't insist. My next question is: Did you go back to your unit at all, Kranj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was released from the hospital. I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember, because you must have got your military booklet back, what did it say? Were you exempt from further military service? Was it a temporary or a permanent exemption? There were various legal possibilities at the time. Do you remember if you were permanently except from military service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly what was written in the -- in the military book, but it could be temporary -- I'm not really sure. I'm not really sure, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you mentioned the date of your injuries, you mentioned the end of January 1991. Do you know now the exact date of these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was somewhere in January. January, maybe beginning of -- I'm not sure. I can't remember exactly, no. I know I was released in February.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. In February 1991, you returned to Vukovar, and you had no further obligations towards the army, and of course you went back to the house of your parents and stayed there with them. Yesterday, in answering my learned friend's questions, you described the situation you found after an absence of four or five months from Vukovar. Could you please clarify a bit further with respect to that situation which you said you found very unpleasant? You mentioned police and some kind of military being everywhere. Could you clarify further what kind of police and what kind of military did you see in the streets and the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can clarify that. There were a lot of people in the same uniforms, grey uniforms that I already described, that harassed us in Vinkovci, with the same symbols. There were people -- there were soldiers that were showing up in camouflage uniforms as well with the Croatian symbols on. There were some regular police in the blue uniforms, but what -- what changed at the time and very fast that they were not wearing anymore a star on their uniforms. They all had an "sahovnica" at that point. Yeah. There were people that we couldn't recognise, because Vukovar is a small town, and you pretty much see all these people when you -- if you don't know the name, but you would see -- see them somewhere on the street. You would know who they were. But most of these people, first of all, had a different accent. So I would say they were coming from somewhere else, somewhere else in Croatia or -- or their behaviour and, you know, the way they spoke to each other. It was just way, way different than we used to speak in Vukovar. You would see all these cars that were coming and going in. Some of them were already repainted with a kind of a -- kind of camouflage colours on it, no licence plates, even though the police was over there. So that made no sense for a car to be with no plates and you have police around them. But sometime nobody did anything. You -- I've seen a lot of -- I've seen a lot of Kalashnikovs in their hands. I've seen all kind of different weapons. They were pretty close where -- where I used to live, around 50 metres where I used to live, so it wasn't something that I couldn't notice at that point. And they were gathering in a large numbers over there in front of -- if front of that place. They used to be -- that building used to be called a Territorial Defence building, and they would come over there and, you know, they would sing these songs, and there were a couple of coffee bars around, and they were sitting inside. Basically a lot of -- lot of -- a lot of uniformed people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: As far as I was able to understand you, sir, their headquarters were close to your home. You're talking about the national defence department. Was that the one that was in the centre of Vukovar even before these events, where the headquarters were, or where they gathered as you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That building, specific building that I'm describing right now, it was exactly across the street from the old municipality building in Vukovar. So it's centre, centre of the town, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned some songs. Could you please tell us more about what kind of songs they were? Were they provocative? Do you remember what these policemen or paramilitary soldiers were singing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as -- sorry. As far as I can remember, most of the songs were kind of national songs, Croatian songs they would sing about killing Serbs or doing -- well, basically some songs that were old-fashioned songs but just words are changed to fit, I guess, a new environment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You are certainly aware of the term "Ustasha" and what the Ustasha were once in Croatia. Was Croatia from Ustasha times mentioned? Were some of the songs songs that dated back to that period? Was there that kind of provocation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't exactly remember the songs. I know sometimes they were mentioned, yes, but you know, they were openly talking on the streets when they would talk -- when they would walk, they're Ustasha, and, you know, they -- you know, there was no hiding of that kind of fact at that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say they were talking, I assume you mean that the people who arrived in those uniforms, they did not conceal that they were Ustasha or they actually paraded that fact. Is that how I can understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They were not hiding. Some people were just screaming and yelling or doing whatever they want, yeah. But, yes, you could hear, because it was just right over there. I was living -- it was close by. I could see them every day. So, yes, there was no hiding of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Their total numbers, can we agree, were much bigger than in normal times in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can -- I can elaborate on that. I haven't seen ever before so much police in Vukovar. Sometimes before the war or before 1991 you would see maybe a car or two that would pass by sometimes, but you -- you would never see such large numbers of -- of soldiers or anybody dressed in Croatian uniforms or anything like that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. The uniforms you mentioned were different. You said that policemen wore grey uniforms rather than blue ones, grey uniforms like the ones you saw in Vinkovci when you were stopped by policemen, and also military camouflage uniforms with the chequer-board insignia and the Croatian insignia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. There were even some police officers in -- still in the blue uniforms but all what I noticed is all the symbols are changed on their uniforms. Now they all had the "sahovnica" on instead of the star that was on before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You mentioned Kalashnikovs and other weapons. I assume you personally saw those Kalashnikovs. Does that mean that on those occasions when they were in town they were carrying their weapons with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You would -- you would see people walking in the street around that area with weapons. There was no hiding of weapons. And the reason why I would say Kalashnikovs because they were talking about Kalashnikovs. That's why they were -- that's the word that they used. But as far as I remember for my military training, you know, I would -- we had a little bit different guns at that point. Well -- so these ones are kind of different. So I would say not JNA weapons, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You are certainly aware of the location of hotel Dunav in Vukovar, or Danube. Did you see these outsiders who were not from Vukovar staying in that hotel, Hotel Danube?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes, sir. That's totally correct. The hotel was full of soldiers and police, yes. And as far as we understood -- as far as I understood - I'm sorry - some things that were happening in Vukovar it would be the night-time, and all these -- usually they would mention people that come from hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What did you hear happened at night? Were there attacks, people going missing, things like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we heard -- I heard, actually, that -- and I've seen couple of places that were blown up during the nights. I -- some restaurants that -- that were really in the very close proximity where I used to live, yes. I haven't heard any people taken at that point or anybody disappeared, but I heard stories from -- from those people that were close by. These -- the uniformed people that would go at nights and, you know, take the cars from people's houses and stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you hear or know who the owners of the catering establishments that were blown up were? Were they Serbs or Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: These events we've just mentioned, when do you think they started happening in view of the period when you arrived or came back in February 1991? Did this happen as soon as you came back or around that time? Can you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. It was a huge presence of them even at that time when I came back. So February would be already a lot of them there. But the numbers increased as the months went past five. I would say that mostly -- the biggest number I noticed after that was after May 2nd, when the attack on the Borovo Selo happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: One more question. How did this kind of behaviour affect you in view of your particular circumstances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-009 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me and my family, we were really scared at that point, because all this stuff was happening just around our house where we used to live, and plus we were receiving a lot of threatening phone calls, even though comparing to my ethnicity, my mom was Serb and they called so many times and they would threaten and say, "Chetniks, you should leave from here. You should not live here." Yeah. "This is not the place for you. This is going to be big Croatia."

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Unfortunately, I think this is a convenient time to finish for today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Domazet. Could I just remind you that we must allow reasonable time for other Defence counsel, and when we resume tomorrow, I hope you can conclude well within the first period for the benefit of others. Yes. Thank you. We will adjourn now, and we resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
